item.title: North Korea tests cluster warhead on ballistic missile in military trial
item.description: North Korea tested a tactical ballistic missile armed with a cluster bomb warhead as part of a three-day series of weapons trials, state media reported Thursday, capping a burst of provocative launches that drew condemnation from Seoul.

item.title: Pentagon says US ready to resume Iran combat if ceasefire falters
item.description: Hours after a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran took effect, the Pentagon on Wednesday warned that American forces remain prepared to restart combat operations if diplomatic talks collapse, even as fresh Iranian strikes on Gulf Arab states underscored the fragility of the truce.

item.title: Hezbollah vows retaliation as Israeli strikes devastate Lebanon
item.description: Hezbollah condemned what it called Israel's "barbaric aggression" on Wednesday and declared it has the "natural and legal right to resist occupation and respond to its attacks," after Israeli warplanes carried out the deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the current conflict began in March. The statement came hours after an armada of Israeli fighter jets struck more than 100 targets across the country in just 10 minutes, killing over 250 people and wounding more than 1,100, according to Lebanon's civil defense authority.

item.title: Sharif's 'draft' post gaffe raises questions about Pakistan's mediator role
item.description: Pakistan's self-styled role as an independent broker of the US-Iran ceasefire is facing scrutiny on two fronts: a Financial Times report published Wednesday revealing that Washington actively pushed Islamabad to act as a conduit for American proposals, and a viral blunder on social media that suggested Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's diplomatic messaging may have been externally scripted.

item.title: CMS experiment confirms W boson mass matches Standard Model, resolving key anomaly
item.description:
A decade-long effort to precisely weigh one of nature's fundamental particles has culminated in a result that reinforces physicists' best theory of the universe. In a paper published Wednesday in the journal Nature, the CMS Collaboration at CERN reports that the W boson has a mass of 80,360.2 ± 9.9 megaelectron volts — a value squarely in line with the Standard Model of particle physics.

The measurement puts to rest an anomaly that has hung over particle physics since 2022, when the CDF experiment at Fermilab's now-closed Tevatron collider reported a W boson mass of 80,433.5 ± 9.4 MeV — seven standard deviations heavier than predicted. That result raised the tantalizing possibility that undiscovered particles or forces were at work. The new CMS finding, achieved with comparable precision, lands far from the CDF value and instead agrees with the Standard Model's prediction of 80,353 ± 6 MeV.

item.title: UMass physicists link record-energy neutrino to exploding black hole
item.description:
On February 13, 2023, an underwater detector in the Mediterranean Sea registered a subatomic particle that should not have existed. The neutrino, dubbed KM3-230213A, slammed into Earth carrying roughly 220 peta-electron volts of energy — about 100,000 times more than anything produced by the Large Hadron Collider, the world's most powerful particle accelerator. No known cosmic process can account for that much energy.

Now, two independent research teams believe they have found an answer: the explosive death of a primordial black hole, a hypothetical relic from the moments after the Big Bang.

item.title: China vows to speed up moon program as Artemis II heads home
item.description: As NASA's Artemis II crew glides homeward after a historic lunar flyby, China has pledged to accelerate its own crewed moon program, sharpening what has become the defining space race of the 21st century. The four astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft are on track to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off San Diego on Friday, April 10, capping a 10-day mission that returned humans to the vicinity of the moon for the first time since the Apollo era.

item.title: Iran announces alternative Hormuz routes, citing mines in main shipping lanes
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Thursday announced alternative transit routes for vessels navigating the Strait of Hormuz, warning that sea mines in the waterway's primary shipping lanes make traditional channels unsafe for commercial traffic.

"All ships intending to transit the Strait of Hormuz are hereby notified that in order to comply with the principles of maritime safety and to be protected from possible collisions with sea mines...they should take alternative routes for traffic in the Strait of Hormuz," the IRGC said in a statement carried by Iranian state media.

item.title: IRGC orders ships to follow new routes in Hormuz amid ceasefire chaos
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps published a map on Thursday showing alternative shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, citing the risk of naval mines, as a two-week ceasefire with the United States entered its second day with the status of the vital waterway still shrouded in confusion.

item.title: Study: Human land changes drive mountain landslide deaths more than nature
item.description: A sweeping new study published in Science Advances finds that human-driven alterations to the landscape — deforestation, agricultural expansion, and road construction — have a greater influence on mountain landslide deaths than natural factors like steep terrain and heavy rainfall, with the heaviest toll falling on the world's poorest nations.

item.title: Artemis II crew races toward Friday splashdown after moon flyby
item.description: Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen is making history as the first non-American to travel beyond low Earth orbit, riding aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft on the Artemis II mission as the crew speeds back toward Earth after a flyby of the Moon. The 10-day mission, which launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center in Florida, marks the first crewed lunar voyage since Apollo 17 in 1972.

item.title: Trump threatens to resume strikes if Iran breaks ceasefire
item.description:
President Donald Trump late on Wednesday warned that all American military forces deployed near Iran will remain in position and threatened to resume hostilities unless Tehran fully complies with the terms of a fragile ceasefire agreement reached just a day earlier.

"All US ships, aircraft and military personnel — with additional ammunition, weaponry and anything else that is appropriate and necessary for the lethal prosecution and destruction of an already substantially degraded enemy, will remain in place in and around Iran until such time as the REAL AGREEMENT reached is fully complied with," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform shortly before midnight Eastern time.

He added: "If for any reason it is not, which is highly unlikely, then the 'shooting starts' bigger and better, and stronger than anyone has ever seen before".

item.title: Dow surges over 1,300 points after U.S.-Iran ceasefire
item.description: U.S. stocks surged on Wednesday in their best session in a year after the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, raising hopes that a crippling oil shortage could begin to ease. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,325 points, or 2.85%, while the S&P 500 climbed 2.5% and the Nasdaq Composite rose as much as 3.5%. It was the Dow's largest single-day gain since April 2025, when markets rallied after a tariff pause.

item.title: Oil surges past $97 as Iran re-closes Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Oil prices climbed back above $97 a barrel on Thursday and Asian stocks retreated as optimism over a fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire gave way to renewed uncertainty, after Israel launched its largest coordinated strike in Lebanon and Iran moved to re-close the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Goldman Sachs cuts gas forecast after ceasefire but warns risks remain
item.description: Goldman Sachs has warned that global natural gas markets face a prolonged supply shock stemming from Iranian attacks on Qatar's liquefied natural gas infrastructure, even as a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran offers temporary relief. The bank said in an April 2 research note that European gas prices could surge to 75–100 euros per megawatt-hour — roughly double recent levels — if disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz persist beyond April.

item.title: New model suggests dark matter has two particle states
item.description: A team of physicists has put forward a new framework suggesting dark matter may consist of two distinct particle states rather than one, offering a potential explanation for why gamma-ray signals observed at the center of the Milky Way have not appeared in smaller nearby galaxies. The paper, titled "dSph-obic dark matter," was published on Wednesday in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics by Asher Berlin, Joshua Foster, Dan Hooper, and Gordan Krnjaic, all affiliated with the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory.

item.title: IUCN lists emperor penguins as endangered over sea ice loss
item.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature has officially listed emperor penguins as endangered on its Red List of Threatened Species, elevating the iconic Antarctic birds from their previous classification of "near threatened" in a move driven by climate-fueled sea ice loss. The update, announced Thursday, marks one of the most dramatic reclassifications for a polar species in recent years.

item.title: Meta expands CoreWeave deal to $21B, launches Muse Spark AI model
item.description: Meta Platforms made a pair of moves this week to accelerate its artificial intelligence ambitions, launching a new flagship AI model called Muse Spark on Wednesday and announcing a $21 billion cloud computing agreement with CoreWeave on Thursday.

item.title: Chevron projects up to $2.2B Q1 earnings boost from higher oil prices
item.description:
Chevron said on Thursday that higher commodity prices driven by the war in Iran are expected to lift its first-quarter upstream earnings by $1.6 billion to $2.2 billion compared with the fourth quarter of 2025, even as the conflict cut into the company's global production.

The disclosure, made in a regulatory filing, comes a day after rival Exxon Mobil issued a similar update showing the Iran war's dual impact on the world's largest oil producers: surging prices that pad upstream profits, offset by physical disruptions to output across the Persian Gulf.

item.title: UK's Cooper demands toll-free Strait of Hormuz passage
item.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is set to declare on Thursday that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz must remain free of tolls, directly challenging both Iran's efforts to control the waterway and a suggestion from President Donald Trump to establish a joint toll system for the critical passage.

In her annual foreign policy address at Mansion House in London, Cooper will argue that international maritime law forbids levying charges on vessels transiting the strait, which carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas.

"The fundamental freedoms of the seas must not be unilaterally withdrawn or sold off to individual bidders. Nor can there be any place for tolls on an international waterway. Freedom of navigation means navigation must be free," Cooper will say, according to advance excerpts of the speech.
